category: ISIS schematic capture, libraries & design management
description: The Proteus Schematic Capture module (historically ISIS): the mode-based editing toolbar and its object types, wiring and connectivity, hierarchy and sheets, component properties and the tools that edit them in bulk, library and part creation, electrical checking and netlisting to PCB, project-level features such as clips and assembly variants, and the report and graphics outputs.

tools.name: Component Mode / Pick Devices
tools.description: The main placement mode. Pressing P (or the P button in the object selector) opens the Pick Devices library browser, which searches every installed library by keyword and filters by Category, Sub-category and Manufacturer, showing the schematic symbol, the PCB package and whether a simulation model is attached. Picked devices are added to the design's object selector and placed by clicking on the sheet.
tools.usage: Component Mode button on the left toolbar, then P (Pick Devices from Libraries); double-click a result to add it to the object selector

parameters.name: Keywords
parameters.description: Free-text search across device names and descriptions.

parameters.name: Category / Sub-category / Manufacturer
parameters.description: Filters that narrow the library tree.

parameters.name: Schematic Preview / PCB Preview
parameters.description: Shows the symbol and the attached package so the right variant is chosen.

parameters.name: Show only parts with models
parameters.description: Restricts the search to simulatable devices.

tools.example: Component Mode > P > Keywords 'PIC16F877A' > double-click the result > close the picker > click on the sheet to place it.
tools.notes: A part with no PCB package cannot be netlisted to the layout, and a part with no VSM/SPICE model will not simulate — both are shown in the picker's preview panes.

tools.name: Wire placement (follow-me wiring)
tools.description: Wires are drawn without selecting a separate wire tool: click on a pin or an existing wire and Proteus auto-routes a right-angled wire to the next click point, snapping to pins and placing junction dots automatically where a wire ends on another wire. Ctrl while clicking gives a diagonal segment and Esc abandons the wire in progress.
tools.usage: Click the source pin, then click the destination pin (or click intermediate points to fix corners); Ctrl+click for diagonal routing
tools.example: Click the MCU's RB0 pin, click at the corner, click the LED's anode — the wire routes and a junction is added if it lands on an existing wire.
tools.notes: Auto wire routing can be toggled from the Tools menu if you prefer to place every corner manually.

tools.name: Bus placement
tools.description: Draws a bus, the thick line that carries a group of signals. Wires entering the bus need labels that match members of the bus's label range (for example D[0..7] on the bus and D0..D7 on the branches), and Proteus draws the diagonal stub automatically when a wire is terminated on a bus.
tools.usage: Buses Mode button on the left toolbar; click to start, click at corners, double-click to finish
tools.example: Draw the bus, label it D[0..7] with Wire Label Mode, then wire each data pin to the bus and label each branch D0 … D7.

tools.name: Wire Label Mode
tools.description: Attaches a label to a wire or bus, which names the net. Two wires that carry the same label are connected without being drawn together, and bus membership is expressed through labels. The label dialog also carries net properties such as net class assignment and the string used for bus ranges.
tools.usage: Wire Label Mode (or press A over a wire); click the wire and enter the label text

parameters.name: String
parameters.description: Net name, or a bus range such as D[0..7].

parameters.name: Net Class
parameters.description: Assigns the net to a PCB net class so the layout uses the right trace and via styles.

parameters.name: Rotate / Justify
parameters.description: Label orientation and alignment on the wire.

tools.example: Wire Label Mode, click the clock wire, String = SCL, Net Class = SIGNAL, OK.

tools.name: Junction Dot Mode
tools.description: Places or removes an explicit connection dot. Proteus adds junctions automatically when a wire is terminated on another wire, so an explicit dot is only needed to join two wires that merely cross, or to break an unintended connection by removing one.
tools.usage: Junction Dot Mode on the left toolbar; click at the intersection to add, click an existing dot to remove
tools.example: Junction Dot Mode > click where the supply wire crosses the decoupling network to tie them together.

tools.name: Terminals Mode
tools.description: Places the connection terminals that give a net a special meaning or carry it between sheets: DEFAULT (a plain named node), INPUT, OUTPUT, BIDIR, POWER, GROUND and BUS. Power and Ground terminals are global — every terminal carrying the same name is one net across the whole design — and INPUT/OUTPUT/BIDIR terminals map to the pins of a parent sheet's subcircuit.
tools.usage: Terminals Mode on the left toolbar; choose the terminal type in the object selector, then click to place and edit its label

parameters.name: POWER
parameters.description: Global supply terminal; its string (e.g. VCC, +5V, VDD) is the net name.

parameters.name: GROUND
parameters.description: Global ground terminal, net GND by default.

parameters.name: INPUT / OUTPUT / BIDIR
parameters.description: Ports of a child sheet, matched by name to the pins of the parent subcircuit.

parameters.name: BUS
parameters.description: Terminal carrying a bus range between sheets.

tools.example: Terminals Mode > POWER > place on the supply rail > edit the label to +3.3V; every +3.3V terminal in the design is now the same net.
tools.notes: Default power rails (VCC/VDD to +5V, GND to 0) are configured under Design > Configure Power Rails, which is where a supply is retargeted for the whole design.

tools.name: Device Pin Mode
tools.description: Places pin primitives — DEFAULT, INVERT, POSCLK, NEGCLK, SHORT, BUS — used when drawing a new schematic symbol on the sheet before turning it into a device with Make Device. Each pin carries a name, a number and an electrical type that the Electrical Rule Check uses.
tools.usage: Device Pin Mode on the left toolbar; select the pin style in the object selector and click to place
tools.example: Draw a box with 2D Graphics, then Device Pin Mode > DEFAULT > place eight pins, naming and numbering each, before running Make Device.

tools.name: Subcircuit Mode and hierarchy
tools.description: Builds hierarchical designs. A subcircuit block drawn on a parent sheet references a child sheet; the block's pins correspond by name to the INPUT/OUTPUT/BIDIR terminals inside the child. Design > Go To Sheet and the right-click Goto Child Sheet command navigate the hierarchy, and a child sheet can be instantiated several times to repeat a circuit.
tools.usage: Subcircuit Mode on the left toolbar; draw the block, add pins, then right-click > Goto Child Sheet to create and edit the child
tools.example: Draw a subcircuit named FILTER with pins IN and OUT, right-click > Goto Child Sheet, place INPUT/OUTPUT terminals named IN and OUT, and build the circuit inside.
tools.notes: A child sheet used more than once is a repeated block; Proteus flattens it at netlist time and gives each instance its own annotated references.

tools.name: Design Explorer
tools.description: A tree and list view of the whole project: the sheet hierarchy on one side, and the parts, nets and pins of the selected sheet or of the flattened design on the other. Clicking an entry cross-probes to the schematic, and it is the fastest way to answer 'where does this net go' across a multi-sheet design.
tools.usage: Design Explorer tab in the application shell (or Design > Design Explorer)
tools.example: Open the Design Explorer, switch to the flattened view, click net SCL — every connected pin is listed with its part and sheet.

tools.name: Sheet management (Root sheets and Go To Sheet)
tools.description: A Proteus design is a set of root sheets plus the child sheets of any subcircuits. Design > New Sheet, Remove Sheet, Go To Sheet and the sheet tabs manage them, and Design > Edit Sheet Properties sets the per-sheet name, reference and non-physical/simulation-only flag.
tools.usage: Design > New Sheet / Remove Sheet / Go To Sheet… / Previous Sheet / Next Sheet
tools.example: Design > New Sheet to add a second root sheet for the power supply, then use POWER terminals to carry the rails between sheets.

tools.name: Edit Component dialog (properties)
tools.description: The per-instance property editor, opened by double-clicking a part. It sets the reference and value, the PCB package, whether the part is excluded from simulation, from the PCB layout or from the BOM, and the Other Properties text box where arbitrary properties (SPICEMODEL, PACKAGE, Program File, MODFILE, tolerance, MPN) are entered as name=value lines.
tools.usage: Double-click a component; or right-click > Edit Properties (Ctrl+E)

parameters.name: Component Reference / Value
parameters.description: Designator and value shown on the schematic and used in the BOM.

parameters.name: PCB Package
parameters.description: Footprint used when the netlist reaches the PCB Layout module.

parameters.name: Exclude from Simulation / PCB Layout / Bill of Materials
parameters.description: Per-instance flags for parts that exist in only one domain.

parameters.name: Other Properties
parameters.description: Free-form name=value property list, including simulation model and firmware properties.

tools.example: Double-click the MCU > Program File = fw\main.cof, Processor Clock Frequency = 8MHz, PCB Package = DIL40, OK.

tools.name: Property Assignment Tool (PAT)
tools.description: Assigns a property to many objects at once by clicking them, or applies it to the whole design or to tagged objects. The string supports increment tokens, so it can, for example, number a row of connectors sequentially or stamp a net class onto every wire in a block — the standard bulk-edit mechanism in Proteus.
tools.usage: Tools > Property Assignment Tool… (or the PAT toolbar button); enter the string, choose the action and the application scope

parameters.name: String
parameters.description: The property assignment, e.g. `NETCLASS=POWER` or `REF=R#` where # increments.

parameters.name: Action
parameters.description: Assign, Show, Hide or Rename the property.

parameters.name: Apply To
parameters.description: On Click, Local Tagged, All Objects in the design, or Global Tagged.

parameters.name: Count / Increment
parameters.description: Starting value and step for the # token.

tools.example: Tools > Property Assignment Tool > String `NETCLASS=POWER`, Apply To: On Click > click each supply wire.
tools.notes: PAT works on wires and nets as well as components, which is how net classes are assigned in bulk before netlisting to the PCB.

tools.name: Global Annotator
tools.description: Assigns component references across the design. It can annotate only unannotated parts (leaving existing references intact, which is what you want once a PCB exists) or renumber everything from scratch, and it handles the per-instance references of repeated child sheets in a hierarchical design.
tools.usage: Tools > Global Annotator…

parameters.name: Annotate all components / only unnannotated
parameters.description: Full renumber versus incremental fill-in.

parameters.name: Include/exclude child sheets
parameters.description: Whether hierarchical instances are annotated as part of the pass.

tools.example: Tools > Global Annotator > 'Annotate only un-annotated components' > OK, so the new parts get references without disturbing the laid-out board.

tools.name: Electrical Rule Check (ERC)
tools.description: Checks the schematic's connectivity: unconnected pins, nets with only one connection, conflicting output drivers, missing power connections, duplicated references and undefined subcircuit pins. The report is shown in a window with clickable entries that select the offending object, and it must be clean before netlisting to the PCB.
tools.usage: Tools > Electrical Rule Check
tools.example: Tools > Electrical Rule Check > review the report > double-click 'Pin U1(RB3) is unconnected' to jump to the pin.
tools.notes: Deliberately unused pins are silenced by connecting them to a DEFAULT terminal or by giving the part the appropriate pin types in its library definition.

tools.name: Netlist compiler / Netlist to PCB
tools.description: Produces the connectivity data for the PCB Layout module and for external tools. In Proteus 8 and later, schematic and layout are live-linked so the netlist is passed automatically as you wire; Tools > Netlist Compiler still produces a standalone netlist in several formats (including SPICE and Proteus's own), and the live-netlist link can be turned off in favour of explicit batch netlisting.
tools.usage: Tools > Netlist Compiler… (format, scope and output destination); the live link is toggled with Tools > Live Netlist in the PCB module

parameters.name: Output
parameters.description: File, clipboard or the PCB module.

parameters.name: Mode
parameters.description: Physical (packaged, for PCB) or Logical (for simulation and reports).

parameters.name: Format
parameters.description: Proteus, SPICE, Tango, EEdesigner, Valid, Multiwire and other supported netlist formats.

tools.example: Tools > Netlist Compiler > Mode: Physical, Format: SPICE, Output: File > save sensor.sdf.
tools.notes: With live netlisting off, the PCB module disables some menu commands until the netlist is brought back in sync.

tools.name: Bill of Materials
tools.description: Generates a parts list from the schematic's components and properties, in HTML, PDF, CSV or Excel form, with configurable columns and grouping and with per-variant output when assembly variants are in use. Parts flagged 'Exclude from Bill of Materials' are omitted.
tools.usage: Tools > Bill of Materials > HTML / PDF / CSV / Excel; configure columns in the BOM setup
tools.example: Tools > Bill of Materials > Excel Output — the spreadsheet opens with reference, quantity, value, package and any custom property columns.

tools.name: Make Device
tools.description: Turns graphics and pins drawn on the schematic into a reusable library device. The wizard steps through the device name and reference prefix, the package assignment (through the Visual Packaging Tool), the component properties stored in the master library part, the datasheet and help topic links, and finally the library to save into.
tools.usage: Select the drawn symbol > Library > Make Device… (or right-click > Make Device)

parameters.name: Device Name / Reference Prefix
parameters.description: Library name and the designator prefix (U, R, C…).

parameters.name: Packagings
parameters.description: One or more PCB packages assigned through the Visual Packaging Tool.

parameters.name: Component Properties
parameters.description: Properties stored with the master part, such as PACKAGE, SPICEMODEL or RoHS status.

parameters.name: Save to library
parameters.description: Which user library the device is written into.

tools.example: Draw the body and pins, select all, Library > Make Device > name 'MYSENSOR', prefix U, assign package SOP18 in the packaging tool, add a RoHS property, save to USERDVC.
tools.notes: Always save user devices into a user library, not into a shipped Labcenter library, so an update does not overwrite them.

tools.name: Visual Packaging Tool
tools.description: The graphical pin-to-pad mapping editor used inside Make Device and when re-packaging an existing part. It shows the chosen footprint with its pads and the device's pin list, and lets each schematic pin be assigned to a pad by clicking, with support for multiple packagings and for gate/heterogeneous parts.
tools.usage: Invoked from the Make Device wizard's packaging step, or Library > Packaging Tool for an existing device
tools.example: Packaging Tool > Add > keyword SOP18 > double-click the package > click each pin then its pad > Assign Package.
tools.notes: Unassigned pins are reported by the tool; a partially packaged device will fail when the netlist reaches the PCB module.

tools.name: Make Symbol
tools.description: Saves selected 2D graphics as a named symbol in a symbol library, so it can be reused as a graphic element — company logos, standard markers, custom terminal or pin shapes, and the graphics used to build device bodies.
tools.usage: Select the graphics > Library > Make Symbol…
tools.example: Draw the company logo with 2D graphics, select it, Library > Make Symbol > name 'LOGO' > save; place it later from the Symbols mode.

tools.name: Library Manager
tools.description: Manages the installed device, package and symbol libraries: browsing and comparing their contents, copying parts between libraries, renaming and deleting, and (in recent releases) linking a controlled library to a Git or Subversion checkout so every part carries its own revision information and library changes are versioned like code.
tools.usage: Library > Library Manager…
tools.example: Library Manager > select the shipped part and the user part side by side > Compare > copy the corrected footprint into the user library > commit the change through the integrated repository view.

tools.name: 2D Graphics modes
tools.description: The non-electrical drawing set: 2D Graphic Line, Box, Circle, Arc, Closed Path, Text and Symbol modes, plus Markers used when authoring devices (origin, label positions). They build device bodies, annotate the schematic and draw board outlines in the PCB module, and carry a selectable graphics style.
tools.usage: The 2D Graphics buttons on the left toolbar (Line, Box, Circle, Arc, Path, Text, Symbols, Markers)
tools.example: 2D Graphics Box mode > draw the device body; 2D Graphics Text mode > add the revision note beside the connector.

tools.name: Graphics styles and templates
tools.description: Proteus draws everything through named styles: graphic styles (line colour, width, fill), text styles (font, size, effects) and junction/terminal appearance, all collected in a template. Template > Set Design Defaults, Set Graph Colours and the style editors change the look of a whole design at once, and a template can be loaded from another design.
tools.usage: Template > Set Design Defaults / Set Graphics Styles / Set Text Styles / Set Graphics Text / Apply Default Template / Load Styles From Design
tools.example: Template > Set Design Defaults > change the paper colour and the grid dot colour; Template > Load Styles From Design to copy a colleague's house style.

tools.name: Sheet size and templates
tools.description: Sets the drawing sheet's size (A4-A0 or a user-defined size) and the border and title block supplied by the design template. A company template carrying the frame, title block and default styles is applied to new designs so every schematic looks the same.
tools.usage: System > Set Sheet Sizes…; Template menu for the border and title block
tools.example: System > Set Sheet Sizes > A3, then Template > Apply Default Template to pick up the company frame.

tools.name: Design properties and header block
tools.description: Holds the document-level fields — title, document number, revision, author, date — which the title block displays through special text fields. Setting them once per project keeps every sheet's title block correct and feeds the printed and PDF output.
tools.usage: Design > Edit Design Properties…; the title block reads the fields through <TITLE>, <DOCNO>, <REV>, <AUTHOR>, <DATE> style placeholders
tools.example: Design > Edit Design Properties > Title 'Sensor Node', Doc. No. 'PRJ-014', Revision 'B' — every sheet's title block updates.

tools.name: Project Clips
tools.description: Reusable blocks of design: a clip stores a piece of schematic together with its matching PCB placement and routing, so a standard sub-circuit (a USB front end, a regulator, an MCU core) can be dropped into a new project complete with its layout. It is Proteus's design-reuse mechanism.
tools.usage: Select the schematic (and corresponding layout) > save as a Project Clip; place from the Project Clips browser in a new design
tools.example: Select the regulator circuit and its laid-out block, save as clip 'LDO_3V3', then insert the clip into the next project to get both schematic and routing.

tools.name: Assembly Variants
tools.description: Manages several build configurations of one design: per variant a component can be fitted or not fitted, and the variant flows through to the bill of materials and the assembly outputs. One project therefore covers several product options without duplicating the schematic.
tools.usage: Tools > Assembly Variants…; mark components as fitted/not fitted per variant
tools.example: Create variants 'Base' and 'WiFi'; mark the radio module and its matching network not fitted in Base; generate a BOM per variant.

tools.name: Search and Tag / selection
tools.description: Finds and selects objects by name or property across the design. Search and Tag matches component references, values or property strings and tags every hit, which then becomes the scope for the Property Assignment Tool, for block copy/move/delete or for a style change.
tools.usage: Edit > Search and Tag… (or Tools > Search and Tag); then use Block Copy/Move/Delete or the PAT on the tagged set
tools.example: Edit > Search and Tag > `R*` > every resistor is tagged > Property Assignment Tool > `TOL=1%` applied to Local Tagged.

tools.name: Block edit commands (Copy, Move, Rotate, Delete)
tools.description: Operate on a tagged region of the schematic: Block Copy duplicates a selection (auto-incrementing references), Block Move relocates it with its wiring, Block Rotate turns it, and Block Delete removes it. Dragging a box with the right mouse button tags a region first.
tools.usage: Right-drag to tag a region, then Edit > Block Copy / Block Move / Block Rotate / Block Delete (or the toolbar buttons)
tools.example: Right-drag around the channel, Edit > Block Copy, place three more copies — references increment automatically.

tools.name: Import Legacy Design
tools.description: Converts Proteus 7 and earlier projects into the Proteus 8/9 single-file format, reading the .dsn schematic and its companion .lyt layout and writing a new .pdsprj. It is the migration path for the large body of legacy Proteus designs.
tools.usage: File > Import Legacy Design…; browse to the .dsn and, if present, the .lyt
tools.example: File > Import Legacy Design > select dice.dsn and dice.lyt > choose the new .pdsprj name and location > Import.

tools.name: EDIF and third-party schematic import
tools.description: Reads EDIF 2.0.0 schematic netlists exported by other EDA tools (OrCAD v9.2 and v17 are explicitly supported). The importer parses the file, reports unsupported entities, draws a new Proteus schematic, and then regenerates a netlist from it and compares it against the netlist in the EDIF file so any connectivity difference is listed for correction.
tools.usage: File > Import > EDIF…; review the import log and the netlist comparison
tools.example: File > Import > EDIF > select the OrCAD-exported .edf > review the log > fix the flagged power-net differences (Proteus uses global power nets by default) and re-check.
tools.notes: Power and ground handling is the usual source of differences: Proteus treats power terminals as global, which may not match the source tool's scoping.

tools.name: Export graphics (bitmap, metafile, DXF, PDF)
tools.description: Writes the schematic (or a tagged region) as an image or vector drawing for documentation: Windows bitmap, Windows metafile/EMF, DXF, EPS and PDF. The PDF export needs no printer driver, which makes it the normal way to circulate a schematic for review.
tools.usage: File > Export Graphics > Export Bitmap / Export Metafile / Export DXF File / Export EPS File / Export PDF File
tools.example: File > Export Graphics > Export PDF File > whole design, colour > sensor_schematic.pdf.

tools.name: Print
tools.description: Prints the design to a printer or PDF writer with control over which sheets are printed, the scale, the rotation, mono or colour output, and whether the printout covers the whole design, the current sheet or a tagged region. Print Preview shows the paginated result.
tools.usage: File > Print… / Printer Setup… / Print Preview; Set Output Area to restrict the region
tools.example: File > Set Output Area over the power section, then File > Print > current area, scale 100 %.

tools.name: Configure Power Rails
tools.description: Defines the design's global power nets and which default names map onto them. Unconnected VCC/VDD pins are tied to the configured positive rail and VSS/GND pins to ground, so a design simulates without every supply pin being wired — and changing the rail's voltage here changes it everywhere.
tools.usage: Design > Configure Power Rails…

parameters.name: Power rail name
parameters.description: The net, e.g. VCC/VDD, GND/VSS, or a user-defined rail.

parameters.name: Voltage
parameters.description: The rail's value used by the simulator when it is not driven by a source.

parameters.name: Unconnected power nets
parameters.description: Which default pin names are automatically connected to this rail.

tools.example: Design > Configure Power Rails > VCC/VDD > set 3.3 V so every implicitly connected supply pin sits at 3.3 V.

tools.name: Set Simulation Options / Animation Options
tools.description: System > Set Animation Options controls the interactive display (show wire voltage by colour, show current direction arrows, animation frame rate and single-step time), and System > Set Simulation Options sets the SPICE kernel's tolerances, timestep limits and convergence behaviour. Together they tune both what you see and how the solver behaves.
tools.usage: System > Set Animation Options…; System > Set Simulation Options…

parameters.name: Show Wire Voltage by Colour
parameters.description: Colours wires by their instantaneous voltage during interactive simulation.

parameters.name: Show Wire Current with Arrows
parameters.description: Animated current-direction arrows on wires.

parameters.name: Frames per Second / Timestep per Frame
parameters.description: Interactive simulation speed and resolution.

parameters.name: SPICE options
parameters.description: RELTOL/ABSTOL/VNTOL-style tolerances, iteration limits and timestep controls on the simulator options tabs.

tools.example: System > Set Animation Options > tick 'Show Wire Voltage by Colour' and 'Show Wire Current with Arrows' so the running circuit is readable at a glance.

tools.name: Design Notes / Project Notes
tools.description: A documentation module inside the project for design notes, review records and manufacturing instructions, with predefined report types and data widgets that pull information (board parameters, stackup, part counts) directly from the design so the documentation stays current.
tools.usage: Project Notes tab in the application shell
tools.example: Open Project Notes, choose the fabrication-notes report type, and insert the stackup widget so the note always shows the current layer construction.

tools.name: Cross-probing between schematic and PCB
tools.description: Selecting a component or net in one module highlights the corresponding object in the other, because both modules share the project database. It is always available in Proteus 8 and later and is the main navigation aid when placing and routing against the circuit's intent.
tools.usage: Open the Schematic Capture and PCB Layout tabs side by side; select in either
tools.example: Click the MCU on the schematic and the footprint highlights in the PCB Layout tab ready to be placed.

tools.name: Model Import wizard (SPICE models)
tools.description: Brings third-party SPICE .MODEL and .SUBCKT definitions into Proteus by attaching the file to a part and mapping the subcircuit's node order onto the symbol's pins. The result is a part that simulates with the vendor's own model rather than a generic approximation.
tools.usage: Library > Model Import…; or set the SPICEMODEL and SPICEFILE properties manually in the component's Other Properties
tools.example: Library > Model Import > select opa2277.lib > choose the .SUBCKT > map nodes 1,2,3,4,5 to IN+, IN-, V-, V+, OUT > attach to the symbol.
tools.notes: A mis-mapped node order produces a simulation that runs but gives wrong results; check the subcircuit's header comment for the documented pin order.

tools.name: Simulation log / Messages
tools.description: The transcript of a simulation run: model loading and resolution, netlist warnings, convergence messages, timestep failures and any output from the firmware's debug channel. It is the first place to look when a circuit refuses to simulate, and the Simulation Advisor links common messages to explanations.
tools.usage: Debug > Simulation Log; the Simulation Advisor is reached from the log entries or from the Help menu
tools.example: Debug > Simulation Log > 'No model specified for U3' — add the SPICEMODEL/SPICEFILE properties or mark the part 'Exclude from Simulation'.
